engagement_title: Marlo Quill autumn drop: pull one signature look out of a month shot on two cameras, recover her own inked motifs as artwork that survives at the size it actually prints, and hand back the drop as one editable set she can keep running
vertical: Media, publishing and personal, independent maker and lifestyle creator (small-batch stoneware and a neighbourhood coffee bar), Portland, Oregon
real_brief_anchor: The ledger row carried no quoted posting, so the anchor here is named honestly as a class rather than a single quote: the recurring Upwork and Freelancer.com creator-retainer post in which an independent maker or lifestyle creator hands over a month of self-shot phone and borrowed-camera photographs and asks for one consistent look plus the platform sizes, typically framed as make my feed look like one account and get these ready to post. Those posts are always signed by the creator themselves, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional creator Marlo Quill and the coined studio name Quill and Kiln; no real creator, account, handle, shop or product is named. The ledger's own row (a preset applied across a batch, then cropped) is the thin half of that posting: what the client is actually buying at a monthly retainer is a look she can be recognised by, her own hand-drawn marks made usable, and a post set she can keep editing when the drop date moves. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) makes that fuller commission honest, because an ink-level trace off a photographed page recovers real hand-drawn artwork and HTML authoring returns a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes.
client_one_liner: I shot a month of the autumn drop on my phone and a borrowed camera in every kind of light, it looks like ten different accounts, and the drop goes live in nine days.
client_brief:
Marlo Quill, autumn drop

I make stoneware in a shared studio in Portland and I sell it four times a year, plus I do a coffee-bar collaboration each autumn. Roughly nine thousand people follow me and about a third of what I sell comes straight off my own posts. The drop opens in nine days.

I shot the whole month myself. Some of it is my phone, some of it is a camera a friend lent me for two weekends, and it was shot wherever I happened to be: the studio in the morning, the market on a grey Saturday, my kitchen at night with one bad overhead light. Every frame is fine on its own. Put them together as a grid and it looks like ten different accounts, and that is the thing I keep getting told to fix.

So: one look. Mine, not a filter. It has to still look like a real room and a real person, because that is what people follow me for, and my glazes are the whole product, so if the treatment shifts the clay colours the work is misrepresented. If a frame will not come to the look, tell me and cut it. I would rather post fewer.

I also draw. There are three little motifs I inked on a sketchbook page, a mug, a sprig and a small kiln, and I photograph that page and crop it every time I need one, which looks terrible. I want them as proper artwork I can put anywhere at any size, on my ground colour, on my labels, on the tiles.

Then the drop itself: square for the grid, the taller crop for posts, the vertical for stories, a nine-tile preview so I can see the grid before I commit, and a one-page thing I can send a brand partner. All in one file I can open and change, because my dates always move.

Warm, quiet, autumn. No neon.
price_band_and_audience: A mid-tier creator retainer at 600 to 1,500 dollars a month, creator 22 to 34 and audience the same, buying 38 to 90 dollar stoneware. The band is load-bearing in both directions. The look has to read as one hand and still read as a real room, because this audience follows the person and treats a heavy uniform filter as evidence that the maker is now a brand, which costs conversion directly. Push the other way and leave the month untreated and it reads as careless at a price point where the photograph is the only way to judge a glaze. It also has to stay cheap enough to run monthly: an elaborate treatment that cannot be repeated next drop is the wrong answer even if this month looks superb. The same work at a 200 dollar gallery-ceramics band would correctly be sparser, cooler and shot on seamless, and shipping that here reads as a different maker.

brand_identity.values: One recognisable hand across the whole feed, with real rooms, true glaze colours and her own drawn marks.

assets_supplied.name: marlo_autumn_month/ (18 frames, mixed sources)
assets_supplied.kind: A month of self-shot content: phone frames at 4032x3024 and a borrowed mirrorless body at 6000x4000, covering studio mornings, a grey market Saturday, a coffee-bar collaboration and a night kitchen under one overhead bulb.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything I shot this month. Phone and the borrowed camera, all mixed together, all sorts of light."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Several phone frames were shot in a portrait mode that has already laid depth blur on the subject and a strong tone curve on the scene, so a whole-frame look lands on them differently from the flat camera frames while reporting the same success; and on a number of the horizontal frames the subject sits high and hard against one edge, which is invisible as a problem until a vertical is cut from them. Separately four of the eighteen are burst frames of one moment at the market, so the month contains fewer distinct posts than the grid needs, and three frames are shot straight into a window.

assets_supplied.name: marlo_motifs_page.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: A handheld photograph of her sketchbook open on the studio bench under a warm lamp, three inked motifs drawn on the page: a mug, a sprig and a small kiln.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "My three drawings. I have been photographing this page and cropping it, which looks awful."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: They are monoline brush drawings photographed on textured paper, so each stroke is only a few pixels wide at page scale and the enclosed counters inside the mug handle and the kiln arch are narrower still. A prompt naming the sketchbook returns the page rather than the ink; a prompt naming all three at once returns two of them and silently drops the third while looking entirely plausible; and background removal on a disjoint line drawing collapses to a few hundred opaque pixels.

assets_supplied.name: marlo_captions.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the drop date and time, the piece names and prices, her caption for each planned post, and the coffee-bar collaboration credit exactly as the bar requires it written.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "My captions and the dates. The bar's credit has to be written exactly like that."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the captions run roughly four times the length of the rest, which the tile measure cannot hold at the type size every other tile uses, and the collaboration credit is a fixed string that cannot be shortened or reflowed to make room.

assets_supplied.name: marlo_glaze_swatches.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: A flat frame of six fired glaze test tiles laid out on the bench, shot on the borrowed camera in window light, supplied as the reference for what the clay and the glazes actually look like.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This is what the glazes really look like. Nothing should end up further from this than it already is."

assets_supplied.name: marlo_grid_reference.png
assets_supplied.kind: A screengrab of another maker's feed grid that she likes, supplied only as a proportion and rhythm reference for how the nine tiles sit together.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Roughly the rhythm I want across nine tiles."

assets_supplied.name: quillandkiln_card_template.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The flat press PDF a local printer already runs for her piece cards: a small portrait card carrying a square piece photo at the top, the piece name, a glaze line with a printed round glaze dot beside it, a price, and a fixed maker line with room for the collaboration credit.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The little card that goes in the box with each piece and stands on the market stall. This is the printer's file, the one he already runs."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The card reads as tidy separate fields with a photo well and a round glaze swatch, but the piece name, the glaze line and the price were set as one continuous story flow in a single frame rather than three addressable fields, the round glaze dot is a decorative grouped path rather than a second picture well, and the fixed maker line and the collaboration credit are a second story whose credit sits at an offset that a mapping computed from the shortened mapping readout lands short of and silently drops on the one card it belongs to. The square piece photo at the top is the only real graphic frame. The media box equals the trim with no bleed box present, so a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured from it however the render is called.

assets_supplied.name: quillandkiln_pieces.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Her working piece list for the card run: the piece name, the glaze, the size, the price, a collaboration-credit column and a picture column naming the month frame each piece was shot in.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Every piece I am running a card for, with the glaze and the price and which photo goes with it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three pieces were never shot this drop and their picture cells are simply blank, which no header reveals and which the merge will not complain about; the prices are written inconsistently across rows ($42, 38.00, 72.0, 88); the Kiln Tumbler appears twice at two sizes so naming one file per piece by name collides and silently overwrites; and the collaboration credit is a fixed string present on the Bench Pour-over Set row alone and blank on every other row, so a run that fills it down every card or drops it off the one card fails in either direction.

acceptance_bar: Seen as a nine-tile grid at grid scale, the drop reads as ONE hand rather than as a month of separate frames, and it still reads as real rooms rather than as a filter pass.
The glazes read as the swatch frame says they read. A treatment that shifts the clay or glaze colour away from the fired reference fails even if the frame looks attractive.
A frame that cannot be brought to the look is named and cut, not shipped at eighty percent, and the reason is written down.
The delivered posts are distinct moments. Four frames of one market moment are one post, not four.
No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions, and no crop's returned tradeoff record carries an upscale entry.

Where a vertical could not be cut from a frame without losing the subject, the route actually taken is named per frame, and if new edge pixels were built for it, the built edge carries the same look as the rest of the frame and shows no seam at post scale.

The three motifs are placeable artwork rather than pictures of a sketchbook: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full-canvas rectangle riding underneath, and all three delivered with none quietly missing.
Each motif still reads as itself at the size it actually sits on a tile and on her warm ground, with its counters open and its thin strokes present, not as a filled blob.
The identical motif artwork appears across the tiles, the verticals and the partner page. A motif redrawn or re-cropped per placement fails.

The drop is ONE working file carrying every canvas size, with the captions, the date and the collaboration credit as text she can retype, the motifs as live vector shapes, and every photograph actually present rather than blank.
The collaboration credit appears exactly as written, unshortened, on every canvas that carries it.
One type system across every canvas, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.
A look recipe she can hand to the next person: what the look is, what was applied per frame and why that frame differed, every resize any tool reported, and what to shoot differently next month.

The piece card run produces one card per piece carrying that piece's own price and glaze, page count equalling catalogue row count, rendered at 300 ppi at trim, each card binding its own picture cut from the graded masters rather than one picture repeated, and per-piece files identifiable where the two Kiln Tumbler sizes share a name.
The fixed collaboration credit appears verbatim on the one card it belongs to and on no card it does not, and the pieces with no photograph are handled deliberately rather than left as holes.
Nothing is claimed as press ready with bleed that the supplied card file cannot carry, and the shortfall is reported.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_list_presets, image_apply_preset, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_adjust_dark_portions, image_adjust_light_portions, image_add_grain, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_remove_background, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence, upscale_factor and requires_expand_chain), image_generative_expand, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision in the commission. It sets the signature look, applies it across a month shot on two different bodies and reconciles by hand the frames a whole-frame preset cannot serve, cuts the three post ratios without ever enlarging a source, knocks three finished pieces to transparency for the partner page, and recovers three hand-inked motifs at ink level off a photographed sketchbook page with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not do for you. It also owns the one sanctioned generative call, used only where a vertical cannot otherwise be cut.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The whole drop as one native editable document carrying square, tall and vertical canvases plus the nine-tile grid preview and the partner page, which is the only surface here that does free-form fixed-canvas layout. She edits it herself every drop because her dates move. Every photograph must be pulled down and inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, the motifs go in as inline SVG so they stay vector and stay identical across placements, family and weight are declared on every text element, each root declares its own canvas, and the payload goes by uploaded URL because inlined photography passes the inline threshold at once.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: One type system across the tiles, the verticals and the partner page. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to read as a maker's hand at a 600 to 1,500 dollar retainer rather than as an agency deck. Numeric weights are non-standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call because one bad name kills the kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or it falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the two frames the month does not contain, a quiet autumn texture for the partner page and one filler frame to make the grid rhythm work, IP-clean, at genuine camera scale and with generative-tech candidates excluded. The only readout before licensing is a 240 pixel thumbnail, so the choice is made on very little. The Boards half persists the shareable selects set she approves the drop from, placed within the twelve-per-call cap, with a partial success read as partial.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt including its validator pass, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with recordRange and additionalImageFiles, document_render_layout with createSeparateFiles and resolution
adobe_surfaces.role: The piece card run, the only genuine one-record-per-page job here: one card per piece in the catalogue, the card that goes in the shipping box and stands on the market stall. The printer's flat card PDF is reverse engineered into a live merge template, the field offsets computed from the document's own reconstructed story text rather than the mapping readout, each row's own piece picture cut from the graded masters and bound through a prefixed picture column, and the run has to reach her as proofs whose per-card identity, price and glaze are actually trustworthy, with the fixed collaboration credit surviving on the one card it belongs to and the pieces with no photograph handled deliberately.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The month is raster work with a hard no-enlargement rule, the motifs are vector recovery, and the drop set has to be an authored fixed-canvas document because she edits it herself every season and nothing else in the connector composes free-form layout. The piece cards are the one deliverable that is a genuine one-record-per-page run at volume, which only the merge surface does, so they are planned onto InDesign from the start rather than forced into the authored document. The brief pins the destinations, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable, and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by frame and by role, so that forty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which frame.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by frame and role.

trajectory.action: Preview all eighteen frames and the glaze swatch reference and triage them: which body shot each, which already carry a heavy in-camera treatment, which are shot into a window, where the subject sits inside each frame, and which frames are the same moment.
trajectory.judgement: Eighteen files is not eighteen posts, and a month shot on two bodies is at least two starting points, not one. The swatch frame is the only fixed reference for what the glazes are, so it is read before any look is chosen rather than after.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering source body, existing in-camera treatment, illuminant, subject placement, and moment identity.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the subject and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop, and a shelf line or a bench edge running downhill is the loudest tell in a grid.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Set the signature look: read the available looks, try the serious candidates on the two frames that differ most (one phone morning, one camera night), judge them by eye against the glaze reference and against the band, and pick one.
trajectory.judgement: This is the taste decision the whole engagement rests on and it is made on the hardest pair, not the prettiest. A look that flatters window light and crushes the night kitchen is not a look, it is a filter. The applied look cannot be confined to a region, so any frame it cannot serve whole has to be served another way.
trajectory.produces: A chosen signature look with a written justification against the band, and a named list of frames the whole-frame route cannot carry.

trajectory.action: Take the month to that look, one call per frame, and for the frames the whole-frame route cannot carry rebuild the same destination by hand with confined corrections, recording the parameters applied per frame.
trajectory.judgement: The destination is a grid, not eighteen good pictures, so the frames that get there by a different route still have to arrive at the same place. The glazes are the constraint that stops the look running away: whatever is done, the clay has to stay where the swatch frame says it is.
trajectory.produces: The month at one look, at source scale, with a per frame parameter log and a reason line for every frame that took a different route.

trajectory.action: Settle the finishing texture, grain and warmth, at one setting across the set, and judge the whole thing as a nine-tile grid rather than frame by frame.
trajectory.judgement: Grain and warmth are what make a mixed-source month read as one hand, and they are also what tips it into filter territory. The judgement is made at grid scale because that is the only scale at which the client experiences it.
trajectory.produces: A finished look applied consistently, and a first grid read with any frame that still stands out named.

trajectory.action: Cut the square tiles and the taller post crops, reading the returned tradeoff record and detection readings on every crop.
trajectory.judgement: A confident looking crop is not evidence, and the subject of a maker's frame is often the hands or the piece rather than the person. The reference grid is a rhythm instruction, not a size instruction.
trajectory.produces: Square tiles and taller post crops with every returned tradeoff record retained.

trajectory.action: Cut the vertical crops for stories from the same masters, reading every returned tradeoff record and detection reading rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: A horizontal frame and a vertical destination is the widest aspect jump in the job, and where the subject sits inside each frame decides whether it can be made at all at native scale.
trajectory.produces: Vertical crops with their tradeoff records retained and any frame that could not be cut cleanly named.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the autumn texture and the one filler frame, filter to photography, exclude generative-tech results, license and download at full resolution, then put them beside the graded month.
trajectory.judgement: The choice is made off a small thumbnail, so it is made on composition and subject rather than on colour, which cannot be judged at that size. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: Two licensed, IP-clean, camera-scale frames placed beside the graded set.

trajectory.action: Recover the motifs off the sketchbook photograph: an ink-level selection naming the drawing's own visual properties, one motif at a time, correct polarity, a bounds crop from each selection's own returned bounds, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full-canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word each selection so it takes the ink and not the paper, which polarity to trace, and whether to spend three calls per motif rather than one call for the page. Background removal is the wrong instrument on a disjoint line drawing.
trajectory.produces: Three placeable, scalable, transparent motifs, each traced and cleaned.

trajectory.action: Knock three finished pieces to transparency for the partner page, checking the alpha survives the crops that follow.
trajectory.judgement: A glazed stoneware rim against a warm bench is exactly the kind of edge that goes soft, and a soft rim on the one page a brand partner reads is the wrong place to find out.
trajectory.produces: Three transparent piece cutouts with their edges inspected at full size.

trajectory.action: Cut the per-piece card pictures from the graded masters to the card's photo-well proportion, reading every returned tradeoff record, and reconcile them against the piece list including the rows that were never shot this drop.
trajectory.judgement: A blank picture cell is not an error the merge will raise, so what a card with no photograph looks like is decided here rather than found on the printed sheet, and a piece shot only inside a scene has to be cut down to itself without enlarging past the master. The cards reuse one frame across a piece's two sizes exactly as she does.
trajectory.produces: One card picture per photographed piece at or below source scale with its tradeoff record retained, and a stated treatment for the pieces with no photograph.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's, judged against a maker at a 600 to 1,500 dollar retainer and an audience that follows the person. The weight cannot be inferred from a style name, and the collaboration credit is a fixed string that has to sit somewhere without being shrunk into invisibility.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with a root per canvas: square, tall, vertical, the nine-tile grid preview and the partner page, each declaring its own canvas size, inlining every photograph as image data, placing each motif as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top-left anchored wrapper, and setting family and weight on every text element with the captions, the date and the collaboration credit as live text.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto-sized right-anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed-size set. The design work is where the motifs sit and how the two long captions are handled without shrinking the type on those tiles alone.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML carrying the whole drop, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per-canvas markup for the rest.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at canvas one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per-canvas markup audit for the others.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's card template PDF into a working document and export its interchange form, then read what the conversion actually exposes: how many text frames, how many graphic frames, what each holds, and whether a bleed box exists.
trajectory.judgement: What the printed card looks like says nothing about how the file was set: the round glaze dot that reads like a second picture well may be a decorative path, and the name, glaze and price may be one flowing story rather than three fields. This is also where the bleed question is answered honestly rather than claimed.
trajectory.produces: A working template plus a frame inventory, a mapping strategy chosen from it, and the stated bleed reality of the supplied file.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct the card's true story text from the interchange file, compute every field offset from that string, generate and validate the mapping, prepare the template, then re-export and confirm every expected placeholder is present, including the collaboration-credit slot.
trajectory.judgement: Validation returns valid on offsets computed from a shortened mapping readout and preparation reports success either way, so the only evidence a field landed, and in particular that the fixed collaboration credit did not fall off the end of the flowing story, is finding it in the re-exported document.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholders, credit slot included, are confirmed by inspection rather than by a success message.

trajectory.action: Run the piece list against the template binding each row's own cut picture through the prefixed picture column, render the printer's run at 300 ppi at trim with page count equal to row count, produce per-piece proofs for her, and read what each delivered proof actually contains against its own row.
trajectory.judgement: One picture repeated across every card is what a naive run ships, the naming key has to survive the two tumbler sizes that share a name, a blank picture cell must resolve to the deliberate treatment rather than a hole, and a file's position in a returned list is not evidence of which record is inside it.
trajectory.produces: The piece card run plus per-piece proofs, each verified against its row, its price and its glaze.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board, add the delivered set and the licensed frames within the per-call placement cap, re-sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the look recipe.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success is not a success, and the vector motifs are not boardable so they belong in the recipe instead. The recipe has to be repeatable next month by someone who was not here, which is what a retainer actually buys.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable selects board with nothing silently dropped, and the written look recipe.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether a vertical can be cut from these particular frames at all without either losing the subject or building pixels. On the horizontal frames the subject sits high and hard against one edge on several of them, and where it sits is a property of how each moment was actually shot, not something readable as a problem from the frame. The crop tool answers a vertical request either by emitting a tradeoff that says the crop needs the frame extended first, or by quietly interpolating up to a two times cap and reporting it only as an upscale factor and a tradeoff entry, with a plausible looking result at a plausible size in both cases. Which frames fall into which is only visible after the crop is asked for.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the answer depends on the subject's position in each frame against the destination ratio, and there is no read-ahead and no parameter that prevents the interpolation. Cropping before grading would trade away crop choice for nothing, since the tradeoff still fires. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for the vertical for stories and the acceptance bar's no-enlargement line is a standing trade requirement, not a disclosure that the tool enlarges. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different route decided per frame: recompose the crop off centre so the subject survives at native scale, drop that frame from the vertical set and use another moment, or extend the short axis with the one sanctioned generative call and then re-judge whether the built edge carries the look, which the grading pass never touched.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read the tradeoff record and the detection reading on every vertical rather than the response, re-plan the crop per frame, and for any frame extended rather than cropped, bring the extended master back through the look pass from the start, because the built pixels were never graded, then re-cut and re-inspect the seam at post scale.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A story set that is soft where every other post is sharp, or verticals that quietly show a shoulder and a wall where the piece used to be, on the format that carries a nine day drop announcement.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether a licensed frame actually sits with the graded month once the two are finally next to each other. Before licensing, the only readout is a 240 pixel thumbnail on a public CDN, which is enough to judge composition and subject and nothing like enough to judge the light, the warmth or how far the frame is from the look the month has just been brought to. The full resolution frame, and therefore its true colour, only exists after the license call, which is a purchase and not a preview. Whether the frame can be brought to the look without being pushed somewhere that makes it read as bought is only answerable with both sitting side by side.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not dodge it. Licensing earlier only moves the same purchase earlier, because the graded set has to exist before the comparison means anything, and doing it right first time would mean choosing correctly from a thumbnail that does not carry the information. The orientation filter is dead and long queries return nothing, so the candidate set cannot be narrowed on the qualities that matter either. (b) Nothing states it: the brief never mentions sourced imagery at all, and the client believes she shot the whole month. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is either a second license against a different candidate, which is a fresh cost decision, or a decision to run the partner page and the grid without a bought frame and rebalance the rhythm around what she actually has.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Place the downloaded frames beside the graded tiles at grid scale, judge them as a set rather than alone, and where a frame does not sit, either license a different candidate and repeat the comparison, or drop it and re-plan the nine-tile rhythm and the partner page around the real month, which changes which frames carry which canvases.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A grid whose one bought frame is the only thing anyone notices, on an account whose entire proposition is that it is a real person in a real studio, and a partner page built on a texture that contradicts the look it is meant to be selling.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered motifs survive at the size they actually reproduce. Traced from a photographed sketchbook page they look clean and complete at full canvas, which is the only scale at which anyone has yet seen them. These are monoline brush drawings whose strokes are a few pixels wide at page scale and whose enclosed counters, the gap inside the mug handle and the opening under the kiln arch, are narrower still, so at the size a motif actually sits on a tile the counters can close, thin strokes can merge and the drawing becomes a blob that still reads as clean artwork in any inspection at canvas size. On her warm ground rather than on white it goes further, because the contrast that was carrying the thin strokes is no longer there. Nothing in any tool response reports it.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it. Reproduction size and the real ground colour do not exist until the canvases are composed, and judging a trace at full canvas is the natural and wrong thing to do at every earlier point. There is no parameter on the trace to tune, since it takes no options at all, so it cannot simply be done better the first time. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says she wants the drawings as proper artwork she can put anywhere at any size, which is her goal, not a warning that they fail small, and the acceptance bar sets a standard rather than disclosing an outcome. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the fix is upstream and different: re-prepare the raster so each motif carries more pixels per stroke before tracing, which means a tighter bounds crop per motif rather than one crop of the page, or change the placement, giving the motif more room and less ground contrast to fight, and then re-judge it there.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Look at each motif at its actual placed size on the actual ground rather than at canvas size, re-crop and re-trace the ones that close, clean the viewBox and the opaque ground path again on every new trace, re-check that all three are present rather than two, re-author the HTML around whatever placement size survives, and re-export and re-audit the canvases from the returned markup.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Three hand-drawn marks delivered as artwork she can use anywhere, which turn into dark smudges on every tile and on every label at exactly the size she uses them, on the one deliverable that was supposed to be recognisably her own hand.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each delivered card proof actually carries its own piece's price and glaze, and whether the fixed collaboration credit survived on the one card it belongs to. The template validates and prepares clean, the run returns success and the right page count, and every card is a valid card, but two things are only visible once the files are opened and read against the roster: the collaboration credit sits at the tail of a flowing story whose offset a mapping computed from the shortened mapping readout lands short of, so it is silently dropped from the Bench Pour-over Set card while every other field looks correct, and a multi-record raster proof route hands the files back in an order that does not match the roster while labelling them by row, so a card named for the Kiln Tumbler can hold the Tall price on the Short piece. The two tumbler sizes sharing a name also collide the instant files are named by piece name alone, and a piece whose picture cell was blank binds nothing unless the deliberate treatment was built in.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it: the credit omission is a property of offsets computed against a shortened readout rather than the reconstructed story, and the proof mislabelling is in the response itself, which is the only thing a run that trusts its tools would use to name the files. Computing offsets from the reconstructed story and choosing a per-record delivery route is exactly the work, not a retry. (b) Nothing states it: the acceptance line that the credit appears verbatim and the requirement that a card carry its own price are standards, not disclosures that the merge drops the credit or reverses the order. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different route: recompute every offset from the reconstructed story so the credit slot lands, and deliver either a single trustworthy multi-page run or a per-record loop so identity is guaranteed, then re-check the two tumbler cards and the pieces with no picture.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Recompute the card's field offsets from the reconstructed story text, re-prepare and re-confirm the credit slot by inspection, abandon any raster proof route whose order cannot be trusted for a per-record or trustworthy multi-page route, rename every proof from what is actually inside it, re-check the two tumbler sizes that share a name so the collision does not overwrite, and confirm the pieces with no photograph carry the deliberate treatment rather than a hole. Where a bound picture is the wrong one or a card picture closes too tight at card scale, re-cut it in Photoshop and re-run, which is a loop back to the imaging surface.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A box of piece cards in which the pour-over set is missing the credit the coffee bar requires exactly as written, and a Kiln Tumbler card that prints the Tall price on the Short piece, discovered by a customer who paid for the piece rather than by Marlo.

deliverables.name: The autumn month at one signature look
deliverables.spec: The month brought to one look across two camera bodies and four lighting situations, with the clay and glaze colours held to the fired swatch reference, plus two licensed camera-scale frames graded into the same world. Per frame parameter log with a reason line for every frame that reached the look by a different route, a named and reasoned cut list, and a moment reconciliation so a burst counts as one post.

deliverables.name: Quill and Kiln motif set
deliverables.spec: Three hand-inked motifs recovered from a photograph of a sketchbook page as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full-canvas rectangle riding along, all three delivered with none quietly missing, each holding its counters and its thin strokes at the size it actually reproduces on a tile and on her warm ground. The identical artwork is reused across every placement rather than redrawn per surface.

deliverables.name: Studio piece cutouts
deliverables.spec: Three finished stoneware pieces knocked to genuine transparency with real alpha at the glazed rim, surviving downstream crops without falling back to a filled rectangle, for the partner page and for reuse on labels. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions with its returned tradeoff record retained.

deliverables.name: The autumn drop as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document carrying square, tall and vertical post canvases, the nine-tile grid preview and the partner page, each keeping its own canvas size, with the captions, the drop date and the collaboration credit as live editable text in one licensed type system, the motifs as real vector shapes, and every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference. Delivered with the self-contained source HTML, which is the durable half: she edits the document every drop and the source guarantees the design survives regardless.

deliverables.name: The piece cards as a per-piece merge run
deliverables.spec: The printer's flat card template reverse-engineered into a live InDesign merge template with every placeholder, the collaboration-credit slot included, confirmed present by inspection of the re-exported document, then run against the piece list: the printer's run rendered at 300 ppi at trim with page count equal to catalogue row count in roster order, each card binding its OWN piece picture cut from the graded masters rather than one picture repeated, plus per-piece proofs named from what is actually inside them on a key that survives the two Kiln Tumbler sizes sharing a name, with the fixed collaboration credit appearing verbatim on the one card it belongs to and nowhere else, the pieces with no photograph handled deliberately rather than left as holes, and the bleed reality of the supplied card file reported rather than claimed away.

deliverables.name: Look recipe and selects board
deliverables.spec: A written recipe naming what the look is and how to reach it again next month, what was applied per frame and why that frame differed, every resize any tool reported with the frame it applied to, every frame that was extended rather than cropped, the moment reconciliation and the cut list with reasons, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and actual numeric weight, the minimum size each motif holds at, and what to shoot differently next month, plus the card run's picture-to-piece reconciliation, the pieces with no photograph and how they were handled, and the bleed reality of the supplied card file. Paired with a persistent shareable selects board with nothing silently dropped.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work and which need an authored fixed-canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free-form layout.
Which signature look, chosen on the hardest pair of frames rather than the prettiest, and defended against a band where a heavy uniform filter costs conversion directly.
How to reach the same destination on the frames the whole-frame look cannot serve, since the applied look cannot be confined to a region.
How far the look may move before the glazes stop matching the fired swatch, which is the one thing in the job that cannot be traded.
Whether eighteen files is eighteen posts, and which of the four burst frames is the one that ships.
Which frames to cut entirely, on a client who has said she would rather post fewer, and how to justify each cut.
Crop route per frame for the vertical set: recompose off centre, drop the frame, or extend the short axis with the one sanctioned generative call and re-grade what it built.
Whether to spend three calls per motif on separate ink-level selections or one call on the page, and how to word each selection so it takes the ink and not the paper.
Where and how large the motifs sit, which is a design decision that also decides whether they survive at all.
How to handle two captions that run four times the length of the rest without shrinking the type on those tiles alone.
Whether a licensed frame joins the world the month lives in or reads as bought, judged only once both exist and once a license has already been spent.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged as a maker's hand rather than an agency deck, plus the real numeric weight per family.

Whether the piece cards are a genuine one-record-per-page merge run or another authored canvas, given the printer wants a batch and the card count must equal the catalogue with each card binding its own piece picture cut from the graded masters.

How to compute the card's field offsets, from the reconstructed story text or the shortened mapping readout, so the fixed collaboration credit is not dropped on the one card it belongs to, and which delivery route and naming key carry per-card identity when the two Kiln Tumbler sizes share a name.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the month into a frontier image model and it returns attractive pictures of pottery. IDENTITY: this is her studio, her hands, her market Saturday and her own three inked drawings, and a regenerated frame is a different maker's month; the motifs specifically have to be RECOVERED from her sketchbook rather than reinvented, because a redrawn mug is somebody else's mark. Her glazes are the product, so a generated or drifted colour is a misrepresented 38 to 90 dollar object. SPEC: the deliverable is three post ratios cut from these specific captures with no interpolated pixels, plus a nine-tile grid that has to work as a set, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for; and the piece cards are a one-record-per-page run whose page count must equal the catalogue and whose every card must bind that piece's own price, glaze and picture, which no generated sheet produces or can be verified against. EDITABILITY: the drop set is defined by being editable, because her dates always move and a retainer client cannot re-commission each time. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: can a vertical be cut from this frame at all, does this bought frame sit beside the month, do these counters stay open at the size the motif actually prints.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_preset, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, add_grain, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, remove_background, generative_expand and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls. The crop checkpoint rests on documented findings: crop_and_resize DOES upscale to a hard 2x cap reporting it only as metadata.upscale_factor plus a tradeoffs entry, and it auto-emits a requires_expand_chain tradeoff with pre-filled expand arguments when a cross-aspect crop would clip the subject; generative_expand is verified live (1024x1024 to 2048x1024, up to 4096 px per side, seeds accepted) and is the sole sanctioned generative call. image_apply_preset is confirmed single-image and NOT maskable, which is exactly why the frames it cannot serve need a hand-built route. The motif checkpoint rests on the verified prompt asymmetry (naming the substrate returned the paper cards at 154,926 px, naming the ink's own visual properties returned the strokes at 9,372 px), the verified partial selection on compound marks, the verified collapse of remove_background on disjoint lettering (1,743 opaque px of ~18,000), and the fact that image_vectorize TAKES NO OPTIONS AT ALL, so all tuning must happen in the raster prep. Vector hygiene is real work: traces come back with NO viewBox and an opaque full-canvas rect at path zero. Alpha survives crops at outputFileType png (13,371 partial-alpha pixels preserved). STOCK: renditionURL is confirmed a 240 px CDN thumbnail, the orientation filter always returns zero hits, long queries return nothing, and asset_license_and_download_stock returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, which is the whole basis of the licensing checkpoint. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt with its validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with additionalImageFiles and document_render_layout are verified fully headless and synchronous, with one record per page and page count equal to row count, rendered at 300 ppi at trim; the credit-omission checkpoint rests on the verified findings that generate_indd_mapping_prompt returns a SHORTENED story readout so offsets must be computed from the reconstructed story, that prepare_indd_merge_template reports success whether or not a field actually landed, and that the only evidence a placeholder is present is finding it in the re-exported interchange file; the proof-identity checkpoint rests on the verified finding that multi-record PNG and JPEG output comes back REVERSED while the response labels it by row, with PDF, createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop as the three verified trustworthy routes. PDF-derived frame granularity is not under the agent's control and no bleed can be introduced, so no bleed gate is asserted and the shortfall is reported instead. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search, and the rendition preview is documented as PAGE 1 ONLY. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold at once. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end. BOARDS: persistence verified with a cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling as a deliverable route, no compositing, no OCR, no text-to-image, no photograph reaching Express as a URL, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.
